summary: This Dockerfile sets up a Ubuntu container with Python, pip, and Quarto (a document generation tool). It downloads a specific version of Quarto, extracts it to a standard location, and makes it available system-wide. It then configures Python to run efficiently in containers by disabling bytecode caching and enabling unbuffered output, and finally installs Jupyter and PyYAML as dependencies.

explanations.2: FROM tells Docker which base image to start with — think of it as the operating system you're building on top of. Ubuntu 22.04 is a lightweight Linux distribution.
explanations.5: RUN executes shell commands during the build. The && chains commands so they all run together in one layer. apt-get update refreshes the package list, then apt-get install downloads curl, Python, and pip.
explanations.6: curl downloads a file from the internet (the Quarto executable). The -L flag follows redirects and -o specifies the output filename.
explanations.7: tar -xzf extracts the compressed file; -C specifies where to extract it; --strip-components=1 removes the top-level folder from the archive so files go directly into /opt/quarto.
explanations.8: ln -s creates a symbolic link, which is like a shortcut. This makes the quarto command available anywhere by pointing /usr/local/bin/quarto to the actual binary.
explanations.10: WORKDIR sets the default directory where commands run and where files are placed. It's like cd-ing into a folder for the rest of the container's life.
explanations.13: This environment variable tells Python not to write .pyc bytecode files, which saves disk space since containers don't need those performance optimizations.
explanations.16: This unbuffered mode makes Python print output immediately instead of waiting for a full buffer, so you see logs in real-time when running the container.
explanations.19: pip3 install downloads Python packages; --no-cache-dir discards pip's cache after installation to reduce the final image size.
